study type: hospital-based cross-sectional study with prospective follow-up
cohort: The study included 352 mother-newborn dyads from two major referral hospitals in Mogadishu, Somalia.
finding: The study revealed an alarmingly high perinatal mortality rate of 173 per 1,000 total births, predominantly due to stillbirths, and found maternal age of 22-29 years, primary or secondary education, and delivery via cesarean section to be significant protective factors.
mod_finding: Delivery via cesarean section was identified as a significant protective factor against perinatal mortality.
